name: get_kernel_stacks
description: Live Linux task kernel-stack census on the debugger host, grouped by identical ordered symbols/callsites, D-state groups first. Opt-in bounded worker; no tracing, attach or stop. Root/access is needed for stack files; denied, empty, vanished and truncated data remain explicit. Refresh defaults true, at most once per second; false reads the cache. Use sequence plus refresh=false while paging to detect replacement. group selects task membership. --kernel-pid restricts collection. User stacks remain available through get_stack on already stopped debugger threads.

name: request_system_capture
description: Request one bounded overview CPU profile or fd-flow/syscall capture. GUI: waits for human cost/scope confirmation. Headless: requires explicit agent-scope control or mutate. Never grants general debugger control. Maximum 10 seconds, CPU 99 Hz; one outstanding request, one request per second. FD flow is exact tracing with bounded rings/drains, not a sampled event-rate guarantee.

name: cancel_system_capture
description: Cancel your pending or active capture request. Independent of displayed generation; only the requester or human can cancel. Owner closes tracing/detaches even without further polling.

name: get_system_capture
description: Read current capture request, consent/deadline, cleanup status, resource limits and last 32 audit transitions. Does not renew capture. Pending approval expires in 30 seconds.

name: get_system_capture_result
description: Read the one retained capture by request_id; only its requester may read it. CPU: summary, samples (pages up to 16), or stack; capture_id/revision and sample arguments follow the profile readers. FD flow: completed counter rows, loss and CPU coverage (pages up to 128). No output file or new host job; a new approved capture replaces the previous result.

name: get_layout
description: Read the last GUI layout in UI units: window and buffer sizes, both scales, density, pane rectangles and collapsed tabs, whole toolbar controls and overflow actions, and value/identifier row elision flags. available=false without a GUI publication; never drives rendering.

name: get_graph
description: Neutral graph used by the galaxy and its table peer: bounded nodes, clusters, directed/undirected edges and retained flow pulses. kind is descriptors or redot. scope=current uses the configured descriptor PID scope (and visible GUI projection when present), or the selected process_id engine scene. No attach, tracing or profiling is enabled. First inventory/scene requests can be pending; poll again. IDs are namespaced decimal strings. Table filtering/sorting/folding is presentation only and does not discard model entities.

process_id.description: Redot process routing only; default original process 1

name: get_overview
description: Whole-system overview of this machine, independent of any debug target: uptime, load, per-CPU utilisation, frequency and topology, memory with swap/zswap and pressure, disks, filesystems, network, power and thermals, users, services, installed packages, system info, the top processes (sort/filter/offset as in list_processes, which is the canonical process table) and the collector's own cost. Every value is a number or {state, why}; an unavailable value is never reported as 0. Rates are between this and the previous observation (interval_s). Reads the shared cache without sampling. A first request may be pending until the owner tick; inspect cache group ages and poll. Process detail requests refresh full IO/fd fields on that tick.

limit.description: Rows for processes and sensors, default 10

sort.description: Descending; rss and memory are the same key; age is oldest first, start newest first. Default cpu

user.description: User name, or a decimal uid

match.description: Substring of comm or command line, ASCII case-insensitive; redacted text never matches

offset.description: Skip this many sorted matching rows; replies give next_offset (null on the last page)

redact.description: Hide user names, hosts, kernel/distro, command lines, addresses and private paths in this reply; does not change the shared cache.

name: list_processes
description: The canonical process table: system processes sorted by cpu, rss (memory), io (storage bytes/s), fds, threads, age, start or pid, filtered by user, comm/cmdline substring or state, paged by limit/offset. processes.count is the whole table, matched the rows after the filter, shown this page, next_offset the next page (null when none) and truncated the processes the collector dropped at capacity. Identity is pid plus start_ticks; pgid and sid name the process group and session. Fields this account cannot read (other users' io and fds) are unavailable with the reason. Reads the shared cache without sampling. A first request may be pending until the owner tick; inspect cache group ages and poll. Process detail requests refresh full IO/fd fields on that tick.

sort.description: Descending; rss and memory are the same key; age is oldest first, start newest first. Default cpu

user.description: User name, or a decimal uid

match.description: Substring of comm or command line, ASCII case-insensitive; redacted text never matches

offset.description: Skip this many sorted matching rows; replies give next_offset (null on the last page)

redact.description: Hide user names, hosts, kernel/distro, command lines, addresses and private paths in this reply; does not change the shared cache.

name: get_process
description: One system process by pid with its sockets: CPU %, memory, io, fds, threads, user, cgroup and command line. Reads the shared cache without sampling. A first request may be pending until the owner tick; inspect cache group ages and poll. Process detail requests refresh full IO/fd fields on that tick.

redact.description: Hide user names, hosts, kernel/distro, command lines, addresses and private paths in this reply; does not change the shared cache.

name: get_connections
description: TCP, UDP and unix sockets from sock_diag with owner pid where this account can see it, plus totals. filter by proto, state, socket uid, external remote or queued bytes; page with offset (matched, shown, next_offset). holders lists every visible process holding the socket inode (shared by fork or descriptor passing), up to 8, with holder_count. When the owner needs privilege, owner_hint names the owning uid, whether it is yours, and the visible processes of that uid whose descriptor tables could not be read (the only possible holders this account knows). Reads the shared cache without sampling. A first request may be pending until the owner tick; inspect cache group ages and poll. Process detail requests refresh full IO/fd fields on that tick.

offset.description: Skip this many matching rows; replies give matched, shown and next_offset (null on the last page).

pid.description: Only sockets whose owner is this pid.

state.description: Exact state, e.g. ESTABLISHED, LISTEN, CLOSE_WAIT

external.description: Only TCP/UDP sockets whose remote is neither loopback nor wildcard

queued.description: Only sockets with bytes in the receive or send queue, or listeners with pending accepts (stuck or busy)

redact.description: Hide user names, hosts, kernel/distro, command lines, addresses and private paths in this reply; does not change the shared cache.

name: get_sensors
description: Power and thermals: every hwmon sensor with label, max and crit, GPU busy/power/temperature/VRAM, CPU package power (RAPL) and supplies, plus CPU and disk temperatures. Reads the shared cache without sampling. A first request may be pending until the owner tick; inspect cache group ages and poll. Process detail requests refresh full IO/fd fields on that tick.

name: get_history
description: Recent series from the collector's bounded history (1200 rows; 10 minutes at the 500 ms default): cpu (busy/user/system/iowait %, load1, the collector's own CPU %), per_cpu (busy % per logical CPU), memory (used/available/cached/swap/zswap bytes), psi (some/full avg10 for cpu, memory and io), disks and network (totals and per device bytes/s, disk busy %), processes (cpu_pct and rss of tracked processes: the top 8 by CPU and by RSS on each sample, plus a pid asked for here, for 10 minutes). Values are bucket means over step seconds; null means not measured in that bucket, never zero. times_s are bucket ends relative to the newest sample. The headless overview samples these groups continuously; with a window, rows follow what the window and requests sample. pending until the first row.

seconds.description: Window ending at the newest sample, default 60

step.description: Bucket width in seconds; default the larger of seconds/120 and the sampling interval; widened so at most 600 points return

pid.description: processes only: this process (and start tracking it)

redact.description: Hide user names, hosts, kernel/distro, command lines, addresses and private paths in this reply; does not change the shared cache.

name: get_process_groups
description: Per-application rollup of the process table: by tree (root = topmost ancestor with the same uid and process group, so a launched app with its helpers or a shell job with its children is one row; kernel threads under kthreadd) or by cgroup path. Each group has members, summed cpu_pct, rss, threads, fds and io_bps (with *_unmeasured_members when some members could not be read; unavailable when none could), its root or cgroup, and its busiest member. RSS sums count shared pages once per member. Sorted descending by cpu, rss, threads, fds, io or members; paged by limit/offset with total and next_offset. Reads the shared cache without sampling; poll while pending.

redact.description: Hide user names, hosts, kernel/distro, command lines, addresses and private paths in this reply; does not change the shared cache.

name: list_radios
description: Wi-Fi cards for burrito mode (is it the microwave?): driver, bus, role (in_use, spare, blocked) and why, spectral and monitor capability, rfkill, what each card can contribute, and what is missing. In-use means associated (or up with a link), up with a default route, another interface on the card up, or managed by NetworkManager/iwd/ConnMan/wpa_supplicant/hostapd (read-only checks); such cards are only read passively. Read-only: never changes a card.

name: radio_channels
description: Burrito mode per Wi-Fi channel 1-14 over the last window: which channels the interferer hits and how badly, so an agent can answer 'which channel should my AP use when the microwave is on?'. Per channel (its 22 MHz mask at its true centre): the window that measured it and how fresh (age_ms, watched_s), power, floor, power over the floor, occupied share, the interferer's MHz in the mask, its power over the floor and share of time, impact (blasted >= 20 dB over the floor, grazed >= 6 dB, clean, unseen = not watched), mains_hz; and traffic from a receive-only monitor card if one was chosen (frames/s, airtime estimate, retry share, bad-FCS frames/s, distinct networks and stations: counts only, addresses hashed in memory with a per-session key, never stored or returned). Also the verdict in words, the blast band, per-window detector regions, the least-affected of channels 1/6/11, the sensors' sweep plan and the TX counters of taken cards. Observer-only: never takes or retunes a card.

name: radio_interference
description: Burrito mode verdict over the last window: 2.4 GHz spectral samples (if a spare card was chosen with --radio, root) analysed for mains-rate (50/60 Hz) pulsing, duty cycle, occupied band and Wi-Fi channels hit, with confidence from the measurement; continuous energy without pulsing is 'pulsing not seen' (inverter microwaves look like that). Joined on CLOCK_MONOTONIC with the in-use link's signal, bitrate, retries, channel busy and gateway ping loss (50 Hz). Starts the passive collector if none runs (no card is ever taken by this tool). Receive-only.
